children: completed its first autonomous flight across the U.S., flying more than 4K miles with zero control inputs from its onboard safety pilot.

Leaving Concord, California, the converted Cessna Caravan performed autonomous taxiing, takeoff, route navigation, and landings under remote supervision from Joby’s Autonomy Headquarters in California and Shaw Air Force Base in South Carolina before reaching North Carolina’s Outer Banks, near the site of the first flight by Wilbur and Orville Wright.
The flight demonstrated the aircraft’s ability to navigate high-density areas, high-altitude mountain terrain, and rerouting around severe weather conditions.
“This journey across America offers a glimpse into a new era of aviation,”
JoeBen Bevirt, Founder and CEO of Joby Aviation.
The aircraft is now on its way back to California, making stops along the way, including Washington, DC; Wichita, KS; and Portland, OR.

Shares lurched higher on the news but have since surrendered early gains and dipped back into negative turf as investors booked profits. JOBY continues to be weighed down by concerns over the company’s heavy investments in autonomous flight and challenges to achieve regulatory approval for fully autonomous flight. Shares are down 54% this year in contrast to an 11% gain in the S&P 500.
Separately, Bevirt sold more than 606K shares of Joby stock on Tuesday, according to a

with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission on Thursday. The CEO sold the stock as part of a trading plan adopted on March 5, 2026, and was executed in multiple trades with stock held by The Joby Trust. Bevirt is the beneficial owner of shares within the trust.
